newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale to speak to Japan on Taiwan pork.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale to speak to Japan on Taiwan pork.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said on Monday he will speak to Japanese officials about how Japan's emergency tariff rates are applied to Taiwanese and Canadian pork imports.

"We think there's two problems with the way the system's administered. One is the equity by which the formula is being administered and whether our exports are being treated fairly vis-a-vis exporters from Taiwan," Goodale said in a conference call with reporters ahead of a trade mission this week.
Another issue Goodale plans to address about the tariff, which increases average pork import prices by 24 percent, is that it shorts Japan's market at its moment of highest demand.
Goodale will be in Tokyo and Osaka, Japan, and Jakarta, Indonesia, March 11 to 21 on a trade mission with 50 other Canadian officials from business and government.
Japan introduced the tariff under Genereal Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT) rules and extended them to June.
Japan imported 653,178 tonnes of pork from Canada in 1996, up 12.5 percent from 1995. Canada supplied 6.2 percent of Japan's pork needs in 1996, Canada Pork International (CPI) said.
A CPI official last week claimed Taiwan avoids Japan's emergency pork tariff through false invoicing. Taiwan's Council of Agriculture denied the allegation.
"We believe there's a valid argument that others may have some unfair advantages to the method of administration," Goodale said.
Japan imports about 50 percent of the food it consumes for a total of US$50 billion a year, Goodale added.
